notes.markdown:
Automations get a full designer, AI steps and ready-made templates; the AI call assistant reaches every app; setup,
meetings, failover and the Android app are better.

## New

- **Automations v2.** A new visual designer (Admin, Automations) with a palette of steps, typed forms, an expression
  editor and a trigger picker. New steps cover logic, approvals and notifications, messaging, integrations, calendar
  and data tables, and placing calls. Every automation keeps a run history and can be tested from the designer
  before it goes live.
- **AI steps and budgets.** Automations can use AI to read, summarise and write text and to make AI-driven calls.
  Set spending budgets so AI use stays within a limit you choose.
- **Template gallery.** 18 ready-made automations (Admin, Automations, Templates) install in a few clicks and can be
  exported and shared in the new template format.
- **AI call assistant and call screening.** The assistant answers and screens incoming calls and shows the caller's
  reason live. It is available in the MonoPhone app (a live screening screen, a Live Activity on iPhone, an Android
  notification and a screened calls history), on Apple Watch, the Mac and Windows apps and the web console. A "My
  assistant" card on the app home screen sets it up in three taps. Administrators control it with a company policy
  (Admin, Call assistant).
- **Guided setup, steps 5 to 18.** The setup guide now walks through the rest of a new installation, with ready
  templates, direct links to each page and hints for network and NAT settings.
- **Meetings and several click-to-call widgets.** Run meetings with your company's own keys, and create more than one
  click-to-call widget, each with its own target, number, opening hours, languages and analytics (Admin, Meetings and
  Widgets).
- **Legal hold and active/standby failover.** Place users or data under legal hold so nothing is deleted, across
  recordings, chats and call history. A standby server can take over automatically if the main one fails.
- **Customer timeline and AI agents that do work.** A single timeline shows every call, chat and note for a customer
  (Customers). AI agents can record outcomes, pause recording while card details are spoken, and prepare quotes.
- **Internet-down survival.** If the office internet connection drops, calls between local phones and over backup
  routes keep working. A new page shows the status and what to prepare.
- **Latin America and Mexico first.** Mexican numbers, language and common local providers are now the default
  starting point, and a migration assistant helps move from another system. New guides cover programmable voice and SMS.
- **Contact centre.** Agent scheduling, a preview dialer card, national do-not-call lists and consent tracking, and
  customer details shown to the agent when a call arrives.
- **Google Drive and Gmail in chats.** Share Drive files and email threads in chat conversations.
- **Push-to-talk on iPhone.** Push-to-talk now works through Apple's own framework, with iOS controls, more Shortcuts
  actions and Android quick tiles for push-to-talk and the call assistant.

## Improved

- **Presence and door phones.** Custom statuses are shown correctly to other phones, door phones support digest
  sign-in, and the share of connections reserved for SIP is configurable.

## Fixed

- **MonoPhone for Android no longer crashes when it is opened** on release builds.
- **Several wording fixes** in the console menus and in a few translated texts.
